⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Locale seam — RIGHT, with one caveat that is not a defect.** The five previews read `locale` from `MetadataPreviewProps` (`locale?: string`, already declared at the base). Every registered-preview mount in the product passes the designer locale: `ResourceEditPage` (`PreviewComponent … locale={locale}` inside `MetadataResourceEditPageImpl`, whose `locale` is `useMetadataLocale()`), `EmbeddedItemEditor` (`Preview … locale={locale}`, same hook), `StudioDesignSurface` twice (`InterfacesPillar`'s `Preview` element and `AutomationsPillar`'s `React.createElement(Preview, {…, locale})`, each pillar's `locale` from `useMetadataLocale()`). No other mount of a registered preview exists in `packages/app-shell/src` or `apps/console/src` outside tests. `CelTestRunDialog` reads `useMetadataLocale()`; its only host, `PermissionAdvancedFacets` (mounted by `PermissionMatrixEditor`), passes the `t` that `PermissionMatrixEditor` binds as `translate(k, locale)` from the same hook, so the dialog's chrome and the dry run's two sentences resolve the same table. `testRunCelPredicate` has exactly one production caller (`CelTestRunDialog`, which passes `locale`); the other callers are `celAuthoring.test.ts` cases, which omit it. With no locale, `pickTable(undefined)` selects the en table, so tests and any locale-less mount render the en rows — the base wording, not the key. In the dev preview gallery the five previews follow `?locale=` (the gallery normalises it to `zh-CN` / `en-US` and passes it as the typed `locale` prop), so the hook-read gap disclosed on objectui#10857 does not touch this slice; the dialog is not mounted in the gallery. Caveat: `JobPreview`'s fire-time formatting still reads `useDisplayLocale()` from the provider (en in the gallery) — objectui#9909's seam, untouched here.

2. **Rows — RIGHT.** Parsed from the diff: 128 en rows, 128 zh rows, the same 128 keys, placeholder sets identical on every shared row (`{type}`, `{object}`, `{variant}`, `{target}`, `{path}`, `{capabilities}`, `{language}`, `{label}`, `{reference}`, `{count}`, `{method}`, `{value}`, `{model}`, `{values}`, `{format}`, `{backoff}`, `{duration}`, `{delta}`, `{n}`), no CJK in any en value, CJK in every zh value. Same meaning at every site.

3. **Census and exclusions — RIGHT.** Counts add up: 58 + 19 + 16 + 14 + 20 + 2 + 1 = 130 sites; 57 + 19 + 16 + 14 + 20 + 2 = 128 rows. A literal-and-JSX-text census of the seven head files (comments stripped, every quoted string and JSX text node with letters) finds no remaining sentence-like English chrome. What remains and why it is not chrome: `Frame label="record_header"` / `list_toolbar` / `list_item` / `record_related` / `record_section` / `record_more` (the location keys); `ScheduleLine label="Cron"` (the syntax's name); the `IconHint` chip `name.slice(0, 3)` and `param_${i}` (identifiers); `'HTTP ' + status + ' OK'` (the HTTP status line) and `Bearer ${token}` (a header); `INHERITED_TARGET` (`(inherited from the bound field)`) — read only by `runtimeWidgetFor`, which hands it to `paramDegradesWithoutTarget` as `referenceTo`, never rendered; `typeLabel` (`any`, `ref`, `${…}[]`) and `stubValue`'s ‹string› / ‹format› stubs inside the example-call JSON; the dialog's sample-JSON default, `${label}: ${(e as Error).message}` (the parser's text) and the ` · ${objectName}` separator; `humanizeMs` / `humanDelta` (`5s`, `30s`, `5m`, `2h`, `3d`, `Nms`) — the notation `every` is authored in, accepted as the PR argues. 5. **Pins — RIGHT on substance, one figure flagged.** 64 cases = 32 zh + 32 en, both files mounting the real components under `I18nProvider` in the case's language (`ActionPreview` etc. with `locale={LOCALE[lang]}`; the dialog with `t` bound as `PermissionMatrixEditor` binds it). Every zh expectation is read from the catalogue and guarded by `zhRow` (rejects the echoed key and the en row); every en expectation is `t(key, 'en-US')` / `tFormat(key, 'en-US', vars)`, never a pinned literal. Sites are grouped per mount: a list-shaped case checks every site the mount renders through `expectSites` (e.g. the api-action case carries 45 sites, the agent full case 15, the tool full case 12), and branch-only sites (each `describeHandler` arm, the singular param count, the seven job schedule states, the dialog's four outcomes) get a case of their own; that is how 64 cases reach 130 sites, and the offline cross-check that every row is asserted holds (each key in `rows-en.json` appears in a pin).
